route: Latvia's new Immigration Law of 20 Aug 2026 replaced the 2002 law from 15 Sept 2026. It has no permit for a 45-year-old couple living on investments. Sec. 27(1)(34) grants up to 2 years to a foreigner who can enter visa-free, has 'pietiekami iztikas lidzekli' (sufficient means) and 'ir sasniedzis Latvijas Republika noteikto pensijas vecumu' (has reached Latvia's pension age), so it does not fit age 45. Sec. 27(1)(36) grants up to 5 years for a transfer of at least EUR 150,000 to a state-created alternative investment fund held for at least 5 years plus EUR 10,000 paid to the state budget. That is the nearest route and is modelled here. Health rule: entry requires '3) ir deriga veselibas apdrosinasanas polise' (sec. 6(1)(3)); the minimum is set by Cabinet Regulation 591 of 28 July 2008: policy limit not below 'EUR 42 600 - pieprasot ilgtermina vizu ... vai uzturesanas atlauju' and cover for at least emergency care, inpatient treatment of a life-threatening condition, transport to hospital, and repatriation (points 6 and 7). The regulation will lapse on 2 Dec 2027.
policy: If Latvia (If P&C Insurance), 'Arzemnieku veselibas apdrosinasana' (foreigners' health insurance): limit EUR 50,000 for treatment, tests, chronic-disease flare-ups, transport, repatriation; acute dental pain only EUR 200; deductible EUR 50 per event; price in the first year EUR 55 per person for age up to 64. The policy covers emergency care and critical life-threatening conditions only. It is not comprehensive care.
working: EUR 55 x 2 people = EUR 110 a year; 110 / 12 = EUR 9.17 a month.

eu_citizen_difference: Cabinet Regulation 591, points 4.6-4.7 and 2.7/3.2, exempt EU/EEA/Swiss citizens and their family members from the policy rule (up to 90 days, or longer when employed, self-employed or providing services). Residence of an EU citizen is a registration, not a permit.
spot_check: None found. Other insurers (Balta, BTA, Compensa, ERGO) were not reached: their pages did not give a price without a calculator.
uncertainty: The EUR 9.17 is a floor: emergency and critical care only, EUR 50 deductible, EUR 200 dental, and it is the first-year price (renewal price not stated). A comprehensive private policy would cost far more, but no published price was found, so 'typical_private' is null. Whether permit applications are granted on this policy at renewal, or whether the couple could join Latvia's state-funded system as temporary residents, was not checked. The EUR 150,000 plus EUR 10,000 investment route is a steep entry cost the capital model should treat separately. Who is state-insured in Latvia was not researched.

statutory_must_pay.what: Nothing a couple like this can pay: no public cover is open to a non-working non-EU couple on a temporary permit.

private_plan.insurer: If, ERGO, Compensa Life (the only insurers selling individual policies per the source)
private_plan.terms: Typical individual programmes cover 50-80% of costs up to annual limits (for example EUR 500 specialist and EUR 1,500 inpatient on Compensa's first-year policy). Deductible and waiting periods not stated. Limited to Latvia or the Baltics.
private_plan.pricing: LSM (2021): If about EUR 200 a year first year, up to EUR 500 with inpatient; Compensa Life EUR 169-199 first year, EUR 200-300 by year three; ERGO Priora from EUR 132.48, Priora plus from EUR 294.60. A 2025 broker tender document (search excerpt) shows Compensa Life basic programme at EUR 350 a person. Taken EUR 350 a person a year x 2 / 12 = EUR 58.33 a month. Weak: old and annual-style figures.
